The monolithic Nandi (stone bull) at Lepakshi is one of the largest single-stone sculptures in India and is a masterpiece of Vijayanagara art. Located a short distance from the Veerabhadra Temple, the Nandi is carved from a single granite block and is admired for its artistic elegance and detailed ornamentation. It is one of the most important monuments of Andhra Pradesh and a major tourist attraction.
Hence, the correct answer is

s: Which temple is famous for its beautifully designed pictorial inscriptions in the Vijayanagara style?
x:
The Veerabhadra Temple at Lepakshi, built during the Vijayanagara period, is internationally renowned for its magnificent mural paintings (frescoes), intricate sculptures and architectural excellence. The paintings depict scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas, representing the finest examples of Vijayanagara painting style. The temple is also famous for the hanging pillar, the giant Nandi monolith, and richly carved ceilings. Lepakshi is regarded as one of the greatest surviving centres of Vijayanagara art and architecture.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: According to art critics, the gopurams of which temple in Andhra are more beautiful than the Vittala Temple gopurams of Hampi?

The Bugga Ramalingeswara Temple and the Chintala Venkataramana Temple at Tadipatri are celebrated masterpieces of Vijayanagara architecture. Art historians have praised their richly ornamented gopurams, intricate carvings and sculptural beauty, with some describing them as even more elaborate than the famous Vittala Temple gopurams at Hampi. The temples display the mature artistic style of the Vijayanagara period, characterized by detailed stone carvings, decorative pillars and elegant architectural composition.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Which of the following is the only temple in Andhra Pradesh with two flagpoles?
o: Simhachalam – Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
Yadagiri – Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple

The Simhachalam Temple near Visakhapatnam is famous for its unique architectural and religious traditions. One of its distinctive features is the presence of two Dhwaja Stambhas (flagpoles), making it unique among the major temples of Andhra Pradesh. The temple is dedicated to Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy, an incarnation combining the forms of Varaha and Narasimha. It is also known for the annual Chandanotsavam, when the sandalwood paste covering the deity is removed for public darshan.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
